steps.title: Riesling
steps.body: Riesling covers about 62% of the Mosel's vineyards, and almost all its fine wine. It buds and ripens late, tolerates cold winters, and keeps high acidity. On the Mosel's slate, it gives light, delicate wines with green apple, peach, citrus, flowers and a smoky, slatey mineral edge.

steps.title: Other grapes and style
steps.body: Müller-Thurgau, a cross created in 1882, is grown on flatter land. Elbling, an ancient grape, grows in the Upper Mosel, often for sparkling Sekt. Pinot Noir and Pinot Blanc are increasing. Mosel Riesling is famous for low alcohol, often 7.5 to 10%, with sugar balanced by fierce acidity; but dry styles are growing.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.

steps.body: A Mosel Riesling Kabinett at 8% alcohol shows how wine can be intensely flavoured without weight.

steps.prompt: Why does Mosel Riesling often have low alcohol?
options: Grapes ripen slowly, and some sugar is left in the wine
It's made from unripe white grapes only
steps.explanation: Cool ripening and residual sugar keep alcohol low.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Riesling is about 62% of vineyards and most fine wine
Mosel Riesling is light, high in acidity, often off-dry
Müller-Thurgau and Elbling play supporting roles
